characters.continuity: The Silmarillion, The Lord of the Rings
characters.summary: Anárion was a King of Gondor, fighting alongside his father Elendil and brother Isildur against Sauron's forces. He wielded traditional royal arms and armor in large-scale martial combat.

sources.supports: Basic biographical details, role in the Last Alliance, and death during the Siege of Barad-dûr.

feats.claim: Defended Osgiliath and parts of Mordor during the War of the Last Alliance.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion - Of the Rings of Power and the Third Age

notableResults.citation: The Silmarillion - War of the Last Alliance
notableResults.note: Fought as co-ruler of Gondor in major military victories before being killed by a falling stone during the siege.

unknowns: Specific personal combat feats apart from general military engagement are not recorded in detail.

characters.summary: Ancalagon the Black was the greatest of Morgoth's winged dragons, possessing immense size, destructive fire, and formidable physical durability that required a host of eagles and Eärendil in his flying ship to defeat.
weaknesses: Vulnerability underbelly or special weakness exploited by legendary heroes/artifacts
limitations: Dependent on physical bulk and wings; vulnerable to coordinated aerial attacks from powerful entities

sources.supports: Role as the mightiest dragon, creation by Morgoth, and defeat by Eärendil.

feats.claim: Burst forth from Angband and drove back the host of the Valar in the War of Wrath.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion - Of the Voyage of Eärendil and the War of Wrath

notableResults.opponent: Eärendil (flying in Vingilot with the Eagles)
notableResults.citation: The Silmarillion - War of the Wrath
notableResults.note: Slain after a day-long battle in the sky, falling upon Thangorodrim and breaking the peaks.

campaignTags.claim: Winged dragon with powerful natural flight capabilities.
Colossal dragon capable of blotting out the sun and crushing mountains.

unknowns: Exact mechanics of how Eärendil penetrated his defenses are mythic and metaphorical.

characters.summary: Ar-Pharazôn was the final and most powerful King of Númenor, whose military might compelled Sauron to surrender. He later attempted to assault Valinor, leading to the destruction of his island kingdom.
limitations: Mortal human limitations despite his immense wealth and power

sources.supports: His reign, military expedition to Middle-earth, Sauron's surrender, and the downfall of Númenor.

feats.claim: Landed in Middle-earth with an armada so vast that Sauron's armies deserted him without battle.

notableResults.note: Captured Sauron through sheer overwhelming military intimidation without a fight.
Attempted to invade Aman and was buried beneath falling mountains when Númenor was destroyed.

unknowns: His personal prowess with weapons in single combat is secondary to his political and military authority.

characters.summary: Aragorn is a skilled Dunedain ranger and swordsman who combines elite tracking, masterful blade work, and commanding leadership. He wields the reforged sword Andúril and possesses exceptional physical endurance and willpower.

mechanisms: Elven chain mail and plate armor
High willpower against psychic or spiritual dread

weaknesses: Vulnerable to heavy physical trauma or overwhelming numbers
limitations: Relies entirely on physical weapons and stamina

sources.supports: Background as Chieftain of the Dúnedain, wields Andúril, and leads the armies of Men.

feats.claim: Fought off multiple Nazgûl at Weathertop using fire and a sword.
Wrested control of the Palantír of Orthanc from Sauron's remote will.

notableResults.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring (Film adaptation / Book equivalent)
notableResults.note: Defeated the Uruk-hai leader in a grueling hand-to-hand duel.

campaignTags.claim: Possesses knowledge of athelas and healing arts as king and ranger.

unknowns: Exact limits of his Númenor longevity enhancements in combat scaling.

characters.summary: Aredhel, known as the White Lady of the Noldor, was a skilled warrior and hunter of royal descent. She was adept at navigating dangerous forests and excelled in horsemanship and martial arts.
limitations: Standard Elven physical boundaries; susceptible to betrayal and deceit

sources.supports: Lineage as daughter of Fingolfin, skill as a hunter, and residence in Nan Elmoth.

feats.claim: Traveled through the perilous paths of Gorgoroth and Nan Elmoth independently.

notableResults.note: Struck by a poisoned dart meant for her son while attempting to escape her captor.

unknowns: Specific martial engagements in major wars are sparsely documented compared to her brothers.

characters.summary: Arwen Undómiel is an Elf princess of Rivendell possessing high spiritual authority, foresight, and command over elemental forces through her heritage and items like her horse or ring.
limitations: Limited direct melee combat engagement in standard accounts

sources.supports: Lineage, role in the story, and her assistance to Frodo.

feats.claim: Evaded the Nazgûl while carrying Frodo and successfully conjured the flood at the Ford of Bruinen.

notableResults.note: Swept the Nine Riders away in a torrent of water.

conditional.dependsOn: Proximity to the River Bruinen and use of her horse Asfaloth

campaignTags.claim: Summoned the rushing waters of the Bruinen to sweep away the Nazgûl (Film depiction).

unknowns: Book versus film discrepancies regarding her active magic use versus Glorfindel's role.

characters.summary: Aulë the Smith is one of the Aratar, a Valar deity of crafting, metal, stone, and earth. He possesses godlike mastery over physical matter and created the Dwarves.
limitations: Bound by the decrees of Eru Ilúvatar; cannot impart independent free will without divine sanction

sources.supports: Identity as a Valar, creator of the Dwarves, and smith of the Valar.

feats.claim: Created the Seven Fathers of the Dwarves out of stone before Eru gave them independent life.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion - Of Aulë and Yavanna

notableResults.note: Consistently repaired and built works faster than Melkor could destroy them.

campaignTags.claim: Master craftsman who forged the lamps of the Valar, vessels of Sun/Moon, and the Dwarves.
Possesses supreme divine magic and creation power.

unknowns: Direct combat feats in war are rare, as his domain is creation rather than destruction.

characters.continuity: The Hobbit, The Fellowship of the Ring
characters.summary: Balin was a veteran Dwarf warrior and companion of Thorin Oakenshield, experienced in subterranean warfare, axes, and tactical defense of strongholds.
weaknesses: Vulnerable to being swarmed by superior numbers in enclosed spaces
mobility: Foot travel in subterranean and mountainous terrain
limitations: Aged in his later years during the colonization of Moria

sources.supports: Participation in Thorin's company, expedition to Moria, and fate in the Chamber of Mazarbul.

feats.claim: Survived the Battle of Five Armies and successfully re-established a dwarf colony in Moria before being overrun.
feats.citation: The Hobbit & The Fellowship of the Ring

notableResults.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring - Book of Mazarbul
notableResults.note: Ambushed and killed by an orc archer outside East-gate in Moria.

unknowns: Detailed individual combat tallies during the Lonely Mountain expedition are brief.
